title: Musical family: grandfather Alphonse Cobet and cousins
summary: His grandfather was a clarinet teacher; cousins James and Reese Cobet played with Chris Kelly and Charlie Love, including a Mexico trip.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Were any of your family musicals?
Yes, my grandfather was an old time clarinet player. He was a professor in the Al Jays. Alphonse Cobet.
Did he teach clarinet only or teach other music?
Did he play with any band or something like that?
Yeah, he played in band. In fact, I learned in later years that Manuel Mineta came up under him.
Mm-hmm. And when did he die? Did you know him?
Oh, well that's before my dad. I mean, I was quite a kid. I was too young to remember that. Mm-hmm.
Did he have a good age when he died?
I think he died in his 70s.
He's back quite a way. Did anybody else in your family play?

Yeah, I had several cuts and I had James Cobet used to play. He played with a lot of bands around here like Chris Kelly, Charlie Love. I think they made the first trip to Mexico, old Mexico. Oh, yeah. Him, Charlie Love, James Cobet, little dead on banjo. I just remember the lineup. What did he play?
He was an alto and clarinet player.
James Cobet. Mm-hmm. And there was another cousin, Reese Cobet. He used to play too. Well, he don't play anymore either.
C-O-B-E-R-T-T-E. Cobet. I mean, most of the people around New Orleans, Creole, they call it Cobet. Mm-hmm.
